newsitem.title: ECUADOR: Ecuador decrees Galapagos immigration controls.
newsitem.headline: Ecuador decrees Galapagos immigration controls.

text.p: Ecuador's government has passed an emergency decree controlling immigration to the Galapagos Islands to prevent further environmental damage to the archipelago, Tourism Minister Juana Vallejo said on Wednesday.

The decree is intended to control the number of Ecuadoreans moving from the mainland and to reduce the use of cars on the islands, whose unique fauna inspired 19th century naturalist Charles Darwin to propose his theory of evolution.
"The decree was put into operation some days ago," Vallejo told foreign correspondents.

The United Nations Educational, Scientific and Cultural Organisation recently threatened to put the islands -- Ecuador's main tourist attraction -- on a list of natural habitats in danger unless the government took action.

"We must not ruin what is a protected area. The emergency decree, as well as the UNESCO warning, is aimed at warning the tourists that there are various international organisations interested in saving the islands," Vallejo said.
Hundreds of Ecuadoreans have moved to the Galapagos, bringing plants and animals that are not native to the islands, such as rats, goats and pigs.
The government recently invited hunters to go to the islands and shoot the goats.

"When the islands were declared to be just another province of the country, movement there was accentuated and that has the biggest impact. Without this measure, immigration could generate problems in the future," Vallejo said.
Only 50,000 tourists a year are allowed into the islands.
